prompt: A mono synth uses **last-note** priority. The player presses 60, then presses 64, then releases 64 while still holding 60. What sounds after the release?

options.explanation: Key 60 is still held, so the voice should fall back to it rather than go silent.

options.text: Key 64 keeps sounding until 60 is released
options.explanation: 64 was released; continuing to play it would be a stuck note.
Correct. The note stack is [60, 64]. Removing 64 leaves [60], and the last held key is 60.
A mono synth has one voice. Note priority picks one key.

workedExample:
```
on 60   stack [60]      -> 60
on 64   stack [60, 64]  -> 64
off 64  stack [60]      -> 60
```

Because the synth tracks every held key, releasing the newest one falls back to the previous one. A synth that only remembered the current note would go silent here.

prompt: A mono synth in **low-note** priority receives: on 48, on 55, on 43, off 43, off 48. Which key sounds after each event?

options.explanation: Correct. The lowest held key after each event: {48}, {48,55}, {43,48,55}, {48,55}, {55}.
That is last-note priority. Low-note picks the minimum of the held keys.
After off 43, key 43 is no longer held, so it can't be the target.

workedExample:
Track the set of held keys and take the minimum:

```
on 48   {48}         -> 48
on 55   {48,55}      -> 48
on 43   {43,48,55}   -> 43
off 43  {48,55}      -> 48
off 48  {55}         -> 55
```

Note that pressing 55 doesn't change the pitch at all in low-note mode: 48 is still lower.
